items.body:
# Security & Observability Enhancements

## Context / Spec

# Security & Observability Enhancements

## Objective
Provide comprehensive security hardening and observability infrastructure across the MoonWitness & Empire of the Light ecosystem, ensuring all applications enforce tenant isolation, auditability, and production-grade observability while maintaining compatibility with the seven-world DNA skin system.

## Problem Statement
The monorepo currently lacks unified security and observability primitives. Individual apps implement basic logging and error handling, but there is no shared framework for:
- Centralized audit logging with tamper-evident records
- Tenant isolation enforcement across all data operations
- Security metrics and alerting infrastructure
- Production readiness validation gates
- Integration with the existing DNA skin engine for consistent security UX

## Objectives & Expected Outcomes
- Deploy a shared audit logging service with append-only event storage
- Enforce tenant_id derivation from authenticated principal (never from request body)
- Provide standardized security middleware for all hub routes
- Implement observability dashboards for request tracing, error rates, and security events
- Ensure all model operations (insert/update/delete) write audit events in the same transaction
- Create production readiness gates that verify security and observability compliance

## Functional Requirements
1. **Audit Logging Service**: Shared service that records every model insert/update/delete with changed field names (not values), tenant_id, actor identity, and timestamp in append-only storage
2. **Tenant Isolation Middleware**: Automatic derivation and validation of company_id on every row; fail-closed rejection on legal_hold / retention_until
3. **Security Middleware**: Default-deny auth policy for hub routes; explicit public allowlist (`/health`, `/ready`, onboarding, non-prod `/docs`)
4. **Observability Pipeline**: Structured logging (JSON format), request ID propagation, error boundary reporting, and Prometheus-compatible metrics
5. **Production Readiness Gates**: Automated checks that verify audit logging, tenant isolation, and security middleware are properly configured before deployment

## Non-Functional Requirements
- All audit events must be SHA-256 content-addressed and stored in `data/storage/<digest>`
- Zero secret leakage in logs (redact all `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values carrying keys/secrets/tokens)
- Performance impact < 5ms per request for security middleware
- Observability data must not block primary request flow
- Compatibility with all seven DNA skin worlds (Imperium Lumen, Nexus Paradox, Lunar Chronicles, etc.)

## Scope
- Shared libraries: `@moonwitness/lint` architecture checks, audit logging service, tenant isolation middleware
- Affected apps: dock, headquarter, id, jizz, moonsky, harbor, gate, sentinel, server
- Integration with `@allah/arsy-orm` for embedded PGlite audit event storage
- Compliance with MOONFRAME SKIN ENGINE contract (token domains, motion, responsive behavior)

## Out-of-Scope
- Application-level business logic changes
- Database schema migrations beyond audit event table
- Third-party security tool integration (self-hosted only)
- Client-side secret management (remains server-authoritative)

## User Stories & Use Cases
1. **Developer**: "When I create a new service, the system automatically logs the creation event with tenant context, and I can query audit events without exposing raw data."
2. **Operator**: "When a suspicious operation occurs, the observability dashboard shows the request ID, affected tenant, and security context for investigation."
3. **Operator**: "When a tenant is on legal_hold, all write operations are rejected with a fail-closed error, and the audit log records the rejection."
4. **Designer**: "Security error pages and audit views use the approved DNA skin tokens and composition blocks, ensuring visual consistency across all seven worlds."

## Dependencies & Constraints
- `@allah/arsy-orm` embedded PGlite for audit event storage
- `@moonwitness/ui` composition blocks (header, destination-card, section-heading, route-shell, status-message, state-panel, kicker)
- MOONFRAME SKIN ENGINE contract token domains and invariants
- Existing `data/storage/` content-addressed storage pattern
- `lint:arch` architecture invariant checks
- `pnpm verify:release` full release gate

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Audit logging service is operational and records all model lifecycle events with tenant_id and actor identity
- [ ] Tenant isolation middleware enforces company_id on every row and rejects operations on legal_hold/retention_until tenants
- [ ] Security middleware implements default-deny auth policy with explicit public allowlist
- [ ] Observability pipeline provides structured JSON logging, request ID propagation, and Prometheus metrics
- [ ] Production readiness gates pass: `pnpm verify:fast` and `pnpm verify:release` succeed
- [ ] All seven DNA skin worlds render security and observability UX consistently
- [ ] No `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values carrying secrets reach the browser
- [ ] `pnpm lint:arch` passes with zero warnings for security/observability changes

## Success Metrics
- 100% of model insert/update/delete operations write audit events in the same transaction
- Zero audit events contain unredacted secret material
- < 5ms overhead for security middleware per request
- All quality gates (`pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm contract:check`, `pnpm lint:arch`, `pnpm typecheck`) pass
- Production deployment can be blocked by readiness gate failures

## Design

# Design: Security & Observability Enhancements

## High-Level Architecture

The architecture introduces three new shared layers integrated with the existing MoonWitness ecosystem:

### 1. Audit Log Service Layer
- **Location**: `packages/lint/src/audit-service.ts` (new) + `packages/arsy-orm` integration
- **Pattern**: Append-only event storage with SHA-256 content addressing
- **Storage**: `data/storage/<digest>` per the content-addressed storage contract
- **Event Schema**: `{ id, timestamp, tenant_id, actor, action, resource_type, resource_id, changed_fields, old_values_hash, new_values_hash, ip_address, user_agent }`
- **Transaction**: Every model insert/update/delete writes one append-only event in the same transaction

### 2. Tenant Isolation Middleware Layer
- **Location**: `packages/lint/src/tenant-middleware.ts` (new)
- **Pattern**: Middleware that runs before every route handler
- **Resolution**: `company_id` derived from authenticated principal, never from request body
- **Fail-Closed**: Reject operations on `legal_hold` / `retention_until` tenants
- **Allowlist**: Explicit public routes (`/health`, `/ready`, onboarding, non-prod `/docs`)

### 3. Observability Pipeline Layer
- **Location**: `packages/lint/src/observability.ts` (new)
- **Pattern**: Structured logging, request ID propagation, metrics emission
- **Logging**: JSON format with correlated fields (request_id, tenant_id, span_id, trace_id)
- **Metrics**: Prometheus-compatible counters for requests, errors, security events
- **Tracing**: OpenTelemetry-compatible request spans with baggage propagation

### Integration Points
- **DNA Skin Engine**: Security and observability UX uses `@moonwitness/ui` composition blocks
  - `route-shell.tsx` for security error pages
  - `state-panel.tsx` for audit event browsing
  - `destination-card.tsx` for summary views
  - `section-heading.tsx` for section headers
- **ARSY-ORM**: Audit events stored alongside ORM operations via PGlite
- **All apps**: Security middleware applied at the hub route level; observability configured per app

## Component & Module Structure

### New Packages/Modules
- `packages/lint/src/audit-service.ts` - Audit logging service
- `packages/lint/src/tenant-middleware.ts` - Tenant isolation middleware
- `packages/lint/src/observability.ts` - Observability pipeline

### Modified Packages
- `packages/arsy-orm` - Extended to automatically write audit events on model lifecycle
- `packages/ui/src/blocks/` - Existing composition blocks used for security UX
- `packages/types` - Updated type definitions for audit events and tenant contexts

### Package Boundaries & Responsibilities
- **`@moonwitness/lint`**: Architecture invariants, audit service, tenant middleware, observability pipeline
- **`@allah/arsy-orm`**: ORM operations + automatic audit event injection
- **`@moonwitness/ui`**: UI composition blocks for security/observability views
- **App packages**: Apply middleware and configure observability; no internal logic changes

## Data Models & Relationships

### Audit Event Model
```typescript
interface AuditEvent {
  id: string;                          // SHA-256 digest
  timestamp: string;                   // ISO 8601
  tenant_id: string;                   // Derived from principal
  actor: string;                       // User/service identity
  action: 'CREATE' | 'UPDATE' | 'DELETE';
  resource_type: string;               // e.g., 'service', 'environment', 'key'
  resource_id: string;                 // ORM record ID
  changed_fields: string[];            // Field names that changed (not values)
  old_values_hash: string;             // SHA-256 of previous state (empty for CREATE)
  new_values_hash: string;             // SHA-256 of current state
  ip_address: string;                  // Client or request source
  user_agent: string;                  // Browser/service identifier
}
```

### Tenant Context Model
```typescript
interface TenantContext {
  company_id: string;                  // Derived from authenticated principal
  legal_hold: boolean;                  // Fail-closed rejection flag
  retention_until: string | null;      // Fail-closed rejection flag
  approved_roles: string[];            // Allowed operations for this tenant
}
```

## API Contracts & Interfaces

### Audit Service API
```typescript
// Log a model lifecycle event
auditService.log({
  action: 'CREATE' | 'UPDATE' | 'DELETE',
  resourceType: string,
  resourceId: string,
  changedFields: string[],
  oldValues?: Record<string, unknown>,
  newValues?: Record<string, unknown>,
  actor: string;
})

// Get audit events with filtering
auditService.getEvents({
  tenantId?: string,
  action?: string,
  resourceType?: string,
  startDate?: string,
  endDate?: string,
  limit?: number,
  offset?: number;
})
```

### Tenant Middleware API
```typescript
// Use in route handlers
const tenant = requireTenant();  // Returns TenantContext, throws if fail-closed
const isPublic = isPublicRoute();  // Checks allowlist
```

### Observability API
```typescript
// Start a traced request
observability.startRequest({ path, method, tenantId });

// Log an event within the request
observability.log({ level, message, correlationId });

// Emit a metric
observability.metric({ name, value, labels });

// End the request span
observability.endRequest({ success, error });
```

## Data Flow & System Interactions

### Model Lifecycle → Audit Event Flow
1. User/Service initiates model operation (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE)
2. `arsy-orm` transaction begins
3. Operation executes on PGlite
4. If successful, `auditService.log()` is called with:
   - Action type
   - Resource type/id
   - Changed field names (not values)
   - Old and new value hashes
   - Tenant context (from principal)
   - Actor identity
5. Audit event stored in `data/storage/<digest>` (append-only)
6. Transaction commits (including audit event)
7. Observability pipeline records the event via `observability.log()`

### Request Flow → Security + Observability
1. Incoming request hits hub route
2. `tenant-middleware` runs first:
   - Derives `company_id` from authenticated principal
   - Checks `legal_hold` / `retention_until` - rejects if set
   - Validates route is in public allowlist if anonymous
3. `observability.startRequest()` begins span
4. Route handler executes
5. `observability.endRequest()` finishes span with success/error status
6. Response sent with security headers and observability data attached

### Error Flow
1. Any error during above flows triggers `observability.log({ level: 'error', ... })`
2. Error boundary renders DNA-appropriate error page (using `@moonwitness/ui` StatePanel)
3. Audit event with `action: 'ERROR'` is logged if operation partially completed
4. Fail-closed tenant checks ensure no data leakage on errors

## UI/UX Flows & Design Specifications

### Security Error Pages
- Built from `StatePanel` (`STATE_PARITY` invariant)
- Uses DNA-appropriate skin tokens from `packages/ui/src/theme.css`
- Consistent across all seven worlds (Imperium Lumen, Nexus Paradox, etc.)
- Shows generic error message; detailed logging internal only

### Audit View Component Tree
```
RouteShell
  └─ Kicker (optional)
  └─ SectionHeading ("Audit Log")
  └─ DestinationCard (summary statistics)
  └─ StatePanel (audit event browser with filtering)
      ├─ EmptyState (no events yet)
      ├─ LoadingState (fetching events)
      └─ ErrorState (fetch failed)
          └─ FilterControls (tenant, action, date range)
```

### Observability Dashboard
- Minimalist design using `@moonwitness/ui` tokens
- Time-series graphs for request rate, error rate, security events
- Drill-down by tenant, IP, or action type
- Responsive: wide (desktop), medium (tablet), narrow (mobile), touch modes

## Integration Architecture

### Skin Integration
Each app declares a `SkinRoot`; security and observability views use:
- `SkinScope` for route-specific experiences without duplicate root worlds
- Token-driven utilities from `packages/ui/src/theme.css`
- Consistent component composition via `@moonwitness/ui`

### Cross-Application Consistency
- Security middleware: Same implementation in all apps
- Observability pipeline: Same configuration pattern across apps
- Audit service: Centralized shared service, not duplicated per app
- Tenant isolation: Derived from principal; same logic in all apps

### Error Handling & Failure Scenarios

#### Audit Service Failures
- **Database unavailable**: Cache miss; retry with exponential backoff; event lost but not leaked
- **Append-only violation**: Alert operator; halt non-critical operations until resolved
- **Performance degradation**: Batch events; reduce flush frequency; alert on latency threshold

#### Tenant Middleware Failures
- **Principal resolution failure**: Default-deny; route to `/ready` with authentication required
- **legal_hold edge case**: Log the edge case; require explicit admin override (recorded in audit)
- **Tenant context stale**: Refresh from principal; if still invalid, fail-closed

#### Observability Pipeline Failures
- **Logger unavailable**: Buffer events in memory; flush on recovery; do not block request
- **Metric emission failure**: Best-effort only; do not throw; internal alerting
- **Tracing propagation failure**: Continue without trace context; mark spans as incomplete

## Security & Performance Considerations

### Security
- **Secret redaction**: All `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values carrying keys/secrets/tokens are stripped from logs
- **Tenant fail-closed**: `legal_hold` / `retention_until` always reject; never implicit allow
- **Default-deny auth**: Every hub route needs verified principal; explicit allowlist only
- **Content-addressed storage**: SHA-256 digests prevent tampering; events are immutable
- **No cross-skin state leakage**: Each skin's security UX is independent; no shared state

### Performance
- **Security middleware**: < 5ms overhead per request (middleware only, no DB calls)
- **Audit event writing**: Within same transaction as ORM operation; no additional round-trips
- **Observability logging**: JSON format; batched flush every 1s or 100 events; async
- **Metric emission**: Non-blocking; in-process counters with periodic export
- **Content-addressed storage**: SHA-256 computation only; no external service dependencies

## Observability Strategy

### Logging
- Structured JSON logs with correlation IDs
- Fields: `timestamp, level, message, request_id, tenant_id, span_id, trace_id, action, result`
- Output: Centralized log aggregator (ELK, Loki, or similar)
- Redaction: Automated stripping of secret-carrying environment variables

### Metrics (Prometheus-Compatible)
- `moonwitness_requests_total`: Total requests by method, path, status code
- `moonwitness_request_duration_seconds`: Request latency histogram
- `moonwitness_audit_events_total`: Audit events by action, resource_type, result
- `moonwitness_tenant_violations_total`: Tenant isolation violations (legal_hold, etc.)
- `moonwitness_security_errors_total`: Security middleware errors

### Tracing
- OpenTelemetry-compatible request spans
- Baggage: `tenant_id`, `actor_id`, `correlation_id`
- Propagation: W3C Trace Context (traceparent header)
- Sampling: Probabilistic 10% for high-volume routes, 100% for security-sensitive routes

## Technical Decisions & Alternatives Considered

### Decision: Shared audit service vs. per-app logging
**Chosen**: Shared service in `@moonwitness/lint` with arsy-orm integration
**Rejected**: Per-app logging (violates audit invariants, duplication risk)
**Rationale**: Single source of truth ensures consistency; arsy-orm integration makes audit automatic

### Decision: Tenant ID from principal vs. from request
**Chosen**: Derived from authenticated principal (fail-closed)
**Rejected**: From request body/query parameters (insecure, violates invariants)
**Rationale**: Invariants explicitly state `company_id` derived from principal, fail-closed

### Decision: Append-only event storage vs. mutable audit log
**Chosen**: Append-only in `data/storage/<digest>`
**Rejected**: Database table with UPDATE/DELETE operations
**Rationale**: Tamper-evident; aligns with content-addressed storage contract; simplifies recovery

### Decision: JSON logging vs. text-based logging
**Chosen**: JSON format with structured fields
**Rejected**: Free-form text logs
**Rationale**: Machine-parseable; enables metrics and tracing; standardized across ecosystem

### Decision: SHA-256 digest vs. UUID for audit event IDs
**Chosen**: SHA-256 content-addressed digest
**Rejected**: UUID v4
**Rationale**: Tamper-evident; content-addressed storage pattern; verifiable integrity

## Rules / Invariants

---
contract: "DOCUMENTATION_CONTRACT.md"
id: "PLAN_SECURITY_OBSERVABILITY_ENHANCEMENTS_RULES"
version: "1.0.0"
owner: "engineering"
status: "proposed"
last_verified: "2026-11-05"
---
# Security & Observability Rules

## Security boundaries

- Every hub route is default-deny and requires a verified principal unless it is on the explicit public allowlist: `/health`, `/ready`, onboarding, and non-production `/docs`.
- Derive `company_id` from the authenticated principal for every tenant-scoped row. Never accept tenant identity from request data.
- Reject writes when `legal_hold` is active or `retention_until` has not elapsed. Fail closed when tenant or retention state cannot be verified.
- Authorize global-admin access on each admin route, require a reason, and record the target tenant. Generic CRUD must not expose identity, audit, or credential-bearing models.
- Use `@allah/arsy-orm` with embedded PGlite for persistence. Parameterize SQL values and allowlist dynamic identifiers.

## Audit and storage

- Record one append-only audit event for each model insert, update, and delete in the same transaction as the model change.
- Include changed field names, actor, and principal-derived `company_id`; do not store changed values or secrets in audit events.
- Store audit content using SHA-256 content addressing at `data/storage/<digest>`. Keep stored content write-once.
- Audit failures must fail the model transaction rather than report a successful unaudited write.

## Observability and secrets

- Emit structured logs and propagate request identifiers without placing credentials, tokens, secret values, or raw changed values in logs, metrics, or traces.
- Keep observability best-effort so an exporter failure does not block the primary request, while preserving security and audit transaction failures.
- Restrict metric labels and trace attributes to bounded, non-secret fields. Do not use tenant identifiers or other high-cardinality values as metric labels.
- Keep upstream credentials server-side. Client code must not read `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values that carry keys, secrets, or tokens.

## Delivery constraints

- Use the existing architecture and platform contracts as the source of truth; do not introduce a second ORM, storage model, UI control system, or client-to-hub transport.
- Apply security and observability at shared boundaries where possible. Do not change unrelated application business behavior.
- Measure performance claims and security coverage; do not treat the plan's targets as verified results until tests or runtime evidence support them.
- UI changes must use `@moonwitness/ui`, skin tokens, and the existing route-state patterns. Do not add raw controls, private component-class selectors, or palette colors in app markup.
- Verify relevant contracts, architecture checks, tests, and type checks for each implementation slice. Report checks that were not run.


## Phases

# Tasks: Security & Observability Enhancements

- [ ] #425 Phase 1 — Audit Logging Service Foundation
- [ ] #426 Phase 2 — Tenant Isolation Middleware
- [ ] #427 Phase 3 — Observability Pipeline
- [ ] #428 Phase 4 — Production Readiness Gates & Integration
- [ ] #429 Phase 5 — Documentation & Type Safety
- [ ] #430 Completion Checklist

items.title: Build per-client Booking Page production pipeline from existing approved template
items.body:
# Goal
Convert the **existing real Booking Page** into a versioned, per-client personalized production base. Owner requested that AI Creative + AI Developer + AI QA prepare and internally test each purchased page before Jessie presents it for owner approval. **Do not rebuild from scratch or deliver a generic logo swap.**

## Verified source of truth (2026-10-14)
- `public/booking/index.html` redirects paid `?key` links to `/base-booking.html`.
- `public/base-booking.html` is the canonical booking template; it loads `/assets/booking-base.js`, `booking-template-live.js`, `booking-template-language.js`, `booking-smart-welcome.js`, and a guarded CB Depot-specific enhancement.
- `public/assets/booking-template-live.js` says the emailed private demo is canonical for purchased pages and loads actual model, pricing, slots, backend.
- `public/assets/booking-base.js` already supports branding description, logo, hero, colors, service cards, reviews.
- `public/assets/cb-depot-experience.js` has a CB Depot business-name guard; must not affect other clients.
- `public/booking-demo/index.html` is a request-personalized-demo form, **not** the actual booking engine. Don't mix these up.

## Milestones / acceptance criteria
### A. Baseline and design system
- [ ] Record versioned, frozen stable booking base; keep current live client deployments unchanged.
- [ ] Extract reusable visual slots (header/hero/services/trust/reviews/CTA/form/footer), style tokens, responsive image variants, and typography while preserving booking engine. Client design must support different hero composition, sections, copy, imagery, colors, cards; not only a logo change.
- [ ] Existing demo, CB Depot, buyer URLs and deep links remain functional. No global CB Depot assets or industry-specific copy on another buyer.
### B. Per-sale generation
- [ ] Intake/payment/owner start confirmation required. No assumptions about unknown pricing, areas, services, legal, emails, photos or testimonials.
- [ ] Store explicit `tenant_id` and immutable `base_version` with a versioned client-specific design/config; server derives tenant from authenticated entitlement and resolves the released booking key securely.
- [ ] Produce a **private preview** of that client's unique design. Do not publish it to a live buyer domain before approval.
- [ ] AI Creative prepares client-specific design brief, asset provenance and copy; AI Developer builds/configures the booking and follow-up workflow; AI QA runs automated + real-device acceptance. Jessie coordinates owner review.
- [ ] Separate client agents are not part of owner AI Team. No cross-tenant access.
### C. QA / approvals
- [ ] Test phone, tablet, desktop; no overflow, cut buttons or unreadable consent; real form submission, email notifications and suppression, booking/quote split, estimate and discounts, ZIP/area, follow-up, access permissions, 404 links, accessibility and EN/ES.
- [ ] Owner-only review screen with full preview, QA evidence, **Approve** / **Request changes** and revision notes; keep a traceable audit and rollback. Existing paid revision limits remain respected.
- [ ] Publishing, email sends, customer changes, payments and DNS changes require explicit approval and permitted backend tools; no unrestricted AI writes.
- [ ] Version upgrades do not silently change existing client pages; tested opt-in migrations and rollback.
### D. Pilot
- [ ] One synthetic cleaning business with distinct visual identity, data and copy, fully QA'd end-to-end; verify demo and CB Depot unaffected.
- [ ] Owner approves pilot before enabling autonomous per-sale generation.

## Coordination
Owner Jessie + six internal specialists only, #56. Buyer agents separately provisioned under #67. PR #72 is a read-only intake readiness helper, not a page builder. Other implementation agent owns live Jessie/AI Team functions; avoid simultaneous edits. Keep this issue for the booking-builder implementation and release evidence.

items.title: [P2.2] Postgres schema and migrations + local Docker Compose
items.body:
**Phase 2 — Pipeline** · Parent: #1 · Est. 1 day · Plan §4

Postgres was decided on 2026-09-01. Dev runs the same engine as prod — Postgres in Docker locally, RDS in AWS — so nothing is discovered at deploy time.

### Schema (all five tables land in the first migration)

```
tenants
  id, name, status, created_at
  icp_config          jsonb   -- ICP description, weights, thresholds, routing rules
  api_key_hash        text    -- argon2 hash, never the key itself
  hmac_secret_ref     text    -- Secrets Manager ARN

leads
  id, tenant_id, submission_id (unique per tenant -> idempotency)
  raw_payload         jsonb
  source, received_at, status
  contact_email_hash  text    -- log correlation without PII in logs

assessments
  id, lead_id, tenant_id, created_at
  tier, total_score, dimension_scores jsonb
  extracted           jsonb
  reasoning           text
  confidence          numeric
  missing_information jsonb
  model_id, prompt_version, effort
  input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cost_usd
  latency_ms

routing_events
  id, lead_id, action, destination, dispatched_at, provider_message_id

feedback
  id, lead_id, rater, verdict (good|bad|unsure), notes, created_at
```

### Scope

- [ ] Alembic (or equivalent) migration creating all five tables.
- [ ] `tenant_id` on **every** table, with a `UNIQUE (tenant_id, submission_id)` constraint on `leads` — that constraint *is* the idempotency guarantee.
- [ ] Indexes for the queries the product actually runs: `(tenant_id, received_at)`, `(tenant_id, tier, created_at)` on assessments, `lead_id` on feedback and routing_events.
- [ ] `docker-compose.yml` with a Postgres 16+ service and a documented `DATABASE_URL` for local dev.
- [ ] SQLAlchemy 2.x models mirroring the schema.
- [ ] A seed script inserting the default internal tenant.

### Why these columns exist now and not later

`prompt_version` on every assessment is what makes *"did last Tuesday's prompt change make things worse?"* answerable. Token counts and cost per assessment make per-tenant billing a `SUM`, not a later migration. Retrofitting either is painful; unused columns are free.

### Acceptance criteria

- `docker compose up` + migrate produces a working database in under a minute on a clean machine.
- Inserting the same `(tenant_id, submission_id)` twice raises a constraint violation.
- Migrations run forward and back cleanly.
- No raw email address column — only `contact_email_hash` for correlation (the raw payload jsonb is the single place PII lives, and is covered by the retention work in #37).

**Depends on:** #4.

items.title: feat(gateway): Industry-Standard Hybrid Gateway with BYOG, Multi-Scheme Auth, and Agent OBO Delegation
items.body:
### Overview
Modern production architectures require serving high-volume, low-latency REST clients (browsers, mobile apps, B2B webhooks) and stateful, bursty AI agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, autonomous agent swarms) without architectural drift or separate microservice bloat.

This issue implements a first-class **Hybrid Gateway** combining industry-standard API Gateway capabilities with industry-standard MCP Agent Gateway capabilities, plus an open **BYOG (Bring Your Own Gateway)** SPI for custom enterprise infrastructure.

### Industry-Standard Capabilities to Deliver

#### 1. Multi-Scheme Pluggable Authentication
- **REST Clients**: Support for `JWT` (OAuth2/OIDC claims), `API_KEY` (high-entropy tokens), `DUAL` (auto-detecting JWT vs API key), and `NONE` (public pass-through).
- **AI Agent Clients**: Support for **On-Behalf-Of (OBO) Delegated Identity** combining `agent_id` (verifying the AI runner) with delegated `user_id` & `tenant_id` context.

#### 2. Agentic Security & Tool RBAC
- Scope-based tool access control: AI agents without required scopes are denied execution before entering the backend.
- Whitelist tag filtering (`include_tags`) to prevent accidental internal/admin route exposure.
- Synchronous tool thread-pool execution via `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` to protect the Uvicorn event loop from DoS.

#### 3. Traffic Shaping & Rate Limiting
- In-memory token-bucket / sliding window rate limiting per client IP or API key.
- Graceful `429 Too Many Requests` responses with `Retry-After` headers.

#### 4. Pluggable BYOG (Bring Your Own Gateway) Architecture
- `BaseGatewayAdapter` abstract class allowing developers to supply custom gateways (Kong, Envoy, Traefik, custom Starlette middleware).
- `app.as_gateway_subapp()` exportable ASGI sub-application enabling FastAPI-FastMCP to be cleanly mounted into existing corporate gateways.

#### 5. Gateway Operational Modes
- `GatewayMode.HYBRID`: Unified REST and MCP active simultaneously on single or split ports.
- `GatewayMode.REST_ONLY`: Pure REST microservice mode (MCP stripped).
- `GatewayMode.MCP_ONLY`: Headless Agentic BFF mode (public docs stripped).
- `GatewayMode.BYOG`: Custom developer gateway adapter execution.

### Target Version
`v0.10.0`

items.title: MongoDB: broad :missing=true on missing_params metadata scans every index key and runs a $lookup per match (slower than the value route)
items.body:
## Summary

On MongoDB, a `:missing=true` search answered from `missing_params` metadata (#1984) is much slower than the value-index route when many resources match. The cause is the shape of the query, not the metadata. The metadata route should never be slower than the route it replaces.

## Current behavior

Measured on MongoDB 8.0, single-node replica set, 1 GB WiredTiger cache, 300k Synthea resources (121,890 Observations), on main `5d92c68a5`. The values are the median of 7 warm runs, page with an accurate total. "Off" means `HFS_MONGODB_MISSING_METADATA=false` from #2209, which uses the value-index route.

| query | metadata on | metadata off |
|---|---:|---:|
| Observation `specimen:missing=true` (121,890 matches) | 9.4 s | 0.35–0.56 s |
| Observation `value-quantity:missing=true` (27,059) | 1.9 s | 0.40 s |
| Procedure `reason-code:missing=true` (30,430) | 2.1 s | 0.08 s |
| Condition `abatement-date:missing=true` (2,010) | 140 ms | 35 ms |
| Encounter `reason-code:missing=true` (5,144) | 0.35–0.50 s | 0.04–0.06 s |
| Observation `encounter:missing=true` (0 matches) | 2 ms | 3.0–3.7 s |

Counts (`_summary=count`) behave the same. Totals are identical on both routes. #2206 does not change these numbers, because none of these queries has a positive filter to drive from.

## Evidence

The count for `specimen:missing=true`, from the mongod slow-query log:

```
planSummary: IXSCAN { tenant_id: 1, resource_type: 1, is_deleted: 1, missing_params: 1, last_updated: 1, id: 1 }
keysExamined: 3014906  docsExamined: 121890  nreturned: 1  durationMillis: 9115
pipeline: [ {$match: {$and: [ {tenant_id, resource_type, is_deleted: false},
                               {$or: [ {missing_params: "specimen"}, {missing_params: {$exists: false}} ]} ]}},
            {$lookup: {from: "search_index", let: {candidate_id: {$cond: [...missing → $id, else false]}}, ...}},
            {$match: {"_hfs_missing_present.0": {$exists: false}}}, {$count: "total"} ]
hint: idx_resources_missing_params
```

There are two separate costs:

1. **Unbounded index scan, about 1.0–1.3 s.** `missing_resource_condition` (`crates/persistence/src/backends/mongodb/search_impl.rs:658`) produces an `$or` that is nested under the scope `$and`. With the hint, the planner builds a single IXSCAN with `missing_params: [MinKey, MaxKey]` and filters in FETCH. That reads every key of the type (3.0M keys for 121,890 Observations, about 25 per document) and fetches every match.
2. **Per-document `$lookup`, about 8 s.** `missing_fallback_stages` (`search_impl.rs:666`) runs its `$lookup` for every candidate. That includes documents that have an array, where `candidate_id` is `false` and the subpipeline can never match. It is still one subquery per document.

The same predicates in mongosh against that database:

```
countDocuments({...scope, missing_params: "specimen"})                       58 ms   (covered)
$and:[scope, {$or:[{missing_params:"specimen"},{missing_params:{$exists:false}}]}]   1292 ms (3.0M keys)
$or:[{...scope, missing_params:"specimen"}, {...scope, missing_params:{$exists:false}}]  91 ms (121,890 keys)
```

## Expected behavior

The cost of a metadata-route `:missing=true` search or count scales with the number of matches, not with the number of index keys of the type. It should be at least as fast as the value-index route for broad matches, and keep its current advantage when few resources match (2 ms vs 3 s).

## Suggested approach

- Root the `$or`: copy the scope (`tenant_id`, `resource_type`, `is_deleted`) into each branch, so `{missing_params: X}` and `{missing_params: {$exists: false}}` each get tight bounds. `missing_metadata_hint` (`search_impl.rs:638`) already accepts an `$or` whose branches all reference `missing_params`.
- Only send documents without an array to the `$lookup` fallback. For example, split the pipeline (or `$facet`/`$unionWith`) so the `missing_params: X` branch skips the lookup entirely. Or, when the freshness probe (#1999) already shows that every live document of the type is stamped, drop the `$exists: false` branch and the lookup.
- Add a plan-shape test asserting `keysExamined` is close to the match count for a broad absence. Use `create_backend_with_stable_probes`.

## Scope / out of scope

- In scope: the resource-side `:missing=true` filter and fallback stages for searches and counts.
- Out of scope: the write and storage cost of `missing_params` (#2006 / #2209) and the positive-filter driver (#2004 / #2206).

items.body:
## Background

The Rust sidecar (`candela-sidecar`) currently has no HTTP handler wired up (TODOs #123-125 in `rust/crates/candela-proxy/src/`). PR #152 added `tenant_id: Option<String>` to the Rust `Span` struct (data model parity), but the actual header/Baggage extraction is not implemented.

## Required work

1. **Wire HTTP handler** in `candela-proxy` — implement the actual request handling entrypoint (resolve TODOs #123-125)
2. **Extract `candela.tenant_id`** from W3C Baggage and `X-Candela-Tenant-Id` header, same precedence rules as the Go proxy
3. **Validation**: same `[a-zA-Z0-9\-._]{1,128}` regex
4. **Span emission**: set `span.tenant_id` before writing to storage
5. **Hurl CI gate**: extend `test/functional/run.sh --rust` to run the full `proxy_tenant.hurl` suite against the Rust binary (TENANT-01..07 already written)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `./test/functional/run.sh --rust` passes TENANT-01..07
- [ ] Rust `cargo test` passes including tenant extraction unit tests
- [ ] CI pipeline runs Hurl suite against both Go and Rust binaries

Relates to: #152

items.title: [E6] ETL and data engineering
items.body:
## Summary
ETL and data engineering (phase 2: Product). Scope, ADRs and exit criteria are in the plan section below.

## Plan
- **Goal.** A replayable, idempotent pipeline from raw documents to tenant-scoped, redacted, embedded chunks and analytics.
- **Scope.**
  - Bronze (GCS by sha256); silver (Docling, Presidio, structure-aware chunking with Voyage token counts, Pandera, rejects; Parquet partitioned tenant / dt); contextual headers (Haiku batch, flag); suitability-rule extraction and validation; embed-indexer publishes (chunk identity is the unique 8-column key of deep-dive 05-1 §5.10 including `valid_from`, `parser_version` and `embed_model`; `(tenant_id, chunk_hash, embed_model)` is a non-unique reuse index) and bumps `corpus_version` last.
  - Dagster assets / partitions run daemon-less as Cloud Run jobs from Scheduler, with Postgres run storage (`dagster` database, `fa_dagster`); `dagster dev` locally. Tenant stages run as worker consumers; PUBLIC (EDGAR 497K) runs all stages in-process in `etl-public` and publishes only analytics events. Synthetic per-tenant corpus.
  - dbt gold as `fa_dbt` (`security_invoker` views or incremental models, never full rebuilds); `dbt-bigquery` marts; BigQuery sink with per-tenant authorized views (primary) and row access policies (second layer).
  - ACL change as metadata UPDATE (applier from E5).
- **Arch sections.** deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md#4.7 to #4.11, deep-dive/04-1-key-flows.md#4.14 (flow 2), deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md#5.2, deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.8; ADR-014, ADR-016.
- **Dependencies.** E5.
- **Spikes first.** Docling on the 497K HTML and inline-XBRL tables (chunk sizes measured with Voyage `count_tokens`).
- **Done when.**
  - Re-running the same partition re-embeds zero unchanged chunks (count asserted); an ACL change updates metadata with zero embed calls.
  - Every Pandera failure appears in `ingest_rejects`; no raw document text exists outside GCS bronze (scan test of `documents`, `chunks`, events, BigQuery).
  - `suitability_rules` is populated and validated for the synthetic corpus; `lookup_suitability_rule` returns rows on a real DB.
  - dbt gold models pass the CI assertion that every tenant-schema table has RLS enabled, forced, with policies, and no dbt run does a full-table rebuild of a tenant table; only `fa_tenant_lookup` is `SECURITY DEFINER`.
  - The PUBLIC corpus is written only by `fa_etl_public` (test: a worker attempt is denied by policy and a PUBLIC event on a pipeline topic is sent to `dlq.v1`).
  - BigQuery tables are day-partitioned, clustered by `tenant_id`, with `maximum_bytes_billed` set; a tenant's authorized view returns only that tenant's rows.
  - Fixes G-07, G-39, G-62.

- **Round 4 changes (2026-11-02).**
  - Silver path is `silver/tenant_id=/doc_id=/version=` (was tenant / dt), so erasure deletes by prefix and a parser bump re-parses; chunk identity includes `valid_from` and `parser_version` (ADR-014 amended, ADR-027). Supersedes the "partitioned tenant / dt" wording and the "re-running the same partition re-embeds zero unchanged chunks" bullet: replay after a parser bump re-parses, and unchanged chunk hashes extend `valid_to` with no embed call.
  - Atomic publish: the indexer is the only writer of `chunks`; it embeds outside any transaction, then one transaction per document: advisory lock first, tombstone check, `contract_passed AND scan_passed`, insert or extend chunks, version `active`, cache purge, `processed_events`, `corpus_version` row last (ADR-028, R4-D5; one transaction per document). Every sink (`bq-sink`, silver, contextualizer, indexer) guards with the E5 ledger helper; the silver worker checks before and after writing Parquet.
  - Ingest scan stage in the silver worker: parse-time sanitiser (script and style, comments, hidden or off-screen text, zero-width and bidi characters), deterministic pattern list, then quarantine (`status=quarantined`, bytes under `quarantine/`, never silver or chunks). Model Armor document screening is added by E11 (ADR-036).
  - Quality: Pandera with `PANDERA_VALIDATION_DEPTH=SCHEMA_AND_DATA`; dbt `contract: enforced` on gold tables; Dagster blocking checks are advisory only (the atomic gate is the control; cross-run behaviour UNVERIFIED, tested here); BigQuery `max_time_travel_hours=48` on every dataset including dbt-created ones (idempotent repo-managed DDL plus an assertion); OpenLineage dropped (ADR-014 amended, ADR-034).
  - Validation (2026-11-07, ADR-039): BigQuery time travel is set by the project default `default_max_time_travel_hours = 48` (dbt sets no dataset options), with the per-dataset setting as an assertion (ADR-029 amended). Chunk identity and embedding generations follow ADR-035 as amended (R4-D19 M1).
  - Contextual headers are an ablation arm, default OFF; the baseline B0 is the free structural prefix (title plus section path) written by the chunker (ADR-016 amended). Presidio runs English only.
  - Real connectors move to E11; `source_observations` is E11's table.
  - Added to Done when: #1 with a test double that commits a tombstone immediately before the sink write (N interleavings: zero rows or objects; E12 repeats it with the real worker); #5 on synthetic poison (malformed HTML and PDF, a zip-bomb-like size, injection payloads: none indexed, all in quarantine or the DLQ, consumers continue); #8 (replay a fixture corpus twice after a parser bump: the hash equals a single run, zero resurrection); a planted bad row fails Pandera; the BigQuery `max_time_travel_hours` assertion.

## Architecture
- deep-dive/04-components-and-responsibilities.md#4.7 to #4.11
- deep-dive/04-1-key-flows.md#4.14 (flow 2)
- deep-dive/05-data-model-and-storage.md#5.2
- deep-dive/05-1-rls-indexes-versioning-and-deletion.md#5.8
- ADR-014
- ADR-016

## Tickets
- [ ] E6-T1 Spike: Docling on EDGAR 497K HTML and inline XBRL
- [ ] E6-T2 Scaffold the ETL package and daemon-less Dagster
- [ ] E6-T3 Synthetic per-tenant corpus generator
- [ ] E6-T4 Bronze asset: GCS by sha256, register documents, publish
- [ ] E6-T5 Silver transform: Docling parse, Presidio scrub, chunking
- [ ] E6-T6 Pandera validation, ingest_rejects and versioned silver Parquet
- [ ] E6-T7 silver worker role: consume bronze, emit silver, guard writes
- [ ] E6-T8 contextualizer: Haiku headers (default off), guarded sink
- [ ] E6-T9 Suitability-rule extraction, validation and lookup
- [ ] E6-T10 indexer: atomic per-document publish and lock order
- [ ] E6-T11 Replay, parser-bump and ACL-change tests with zero embed calls
- [ ] E6-T12 Dagster partitions and the etl job entrypoint
- [ ] E6-T13 etl-public: in-process EDGAR 497K pipeline as fa_etl_public
- [ ] E6-T14 Raw-text scan test across documents, chunks, events, BigQuery
- [ ] E6-T15 dbt project and Postgres gold models as fa_dbt
- [ ] E6-T16 CI assertions: tenant tables RLS and no dbt full rebuild
- [ ] E6-T17 BigQuery dataset: partitioned tables, views, 48 h time travel
- [ ] E6-T18 dbt-bigquery marts and the ingest_events feed
- [ ] E6-T19 BigQuery isolation, byte-cap and time-travel acceptance test
- [ ] E6-T20 Ingest scan stage and quarantine in the silver worker

- [ ] E6-T22 voyage-context-4 contextualized chunk embeddings as an eval-only generation

items.title: S3 client panics when S3_CA_FILE holds no PEM certificate

labels.name: stage:done
labels.description: Pipeline opened a pull request for this issue

items.body:
### Describe the bug

When `S3_CA_FILE` points to a file that contains no PEM certificate, `s3.NewReadOnlyClient` logs `error parsing the certificate for minio` and returns a nil client with a nil error. `s3.NewClient`, which the collector, query, and maintain commands reach through `s3.NewClientWithRetry`, then calls `MakeBucket` on the nil client and panics with a nil pointer dereference instead of reporting a bad CA file.

Expected: `NewReadOnlyClient` returns a non-nil error that names the file, for example `parse S3 CA certificate /etc/profiler/s3-ca/ca.crt: no PEM certificates found`, and `NewClient` returns that error without panicking.

### To Reproduce

Add this test to `backend/libs/s3` (I ran it through `go test -overlay`, without changing the tree). No S3 endpoint is needed, because the failure happens before the first request:

```go
func TestReproInvalidCAFile(t *testing.T) {
	caFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "ca.crt")
	if err := os.WriteFile(caFile, []byte("not a PEM certificate\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	params := Params{
		Endpoint:        "minio.example:9000",
		AccessKeyID:     "key",
		SecretAccessKey: "secret",
		UseSSL:          true,
		BucketName:      "profiler",
		CAFile:          caFile,
	}
	mc, err := NewReadOnlyClient(context.Background(), params)
	fmt.Printf("NewReadOnlyClient: client=%v err=%v\n", mc, err)

	defer func() {
		fmt.Printf("NewClient panicked: %v\n", recover())
	}()
	mc, err = NewClient(context.Background(), params)
	fmt.Printf("NewClient: client=%v err=%v\n", mc, err)
}
```

```bash
go test -count=1 -v -run TestReproInvalidCAFile ./libs/s3
```

### Version

`main` at `50d66f10`, Go 1.27.1, darwin/arm64.

### Logs

```text
=== RUN   TestReproInvalidCAFile
[2026-09-14T23:44:59.067] [ERROR] [request_id=-] [tenant_id=--] [thread=-] [class=s3/minio.go:52] error parsing the certificate for minio
NewReadOnlyClient: client=<nil> err=<nil>
[2026-09-14T23:44:59.067] [ERROR] [request_id=-] [tenant_id=--] [thread=-] [class=s3/minio.go:52] error parsing the certificate for minio
NewClient panicked: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
--- PASS: TestReproInvalidCAFile (0.00s)
```

### Additional information

The cause is my reading of the code: the branch at `backend/libs/s3/minio.go:51-53` returns `nil, err`, and `err` there is the nil result of the successful `os.ReadFile` a few lines above.

I have not run a collector with a malformed CA file, so I have not checked what the pod log shows when the panic happens inside `NewClientWithRetry`.

Found during a review of the backend telemetry.

items.title: Azure secrets provider does not authenticate using Client credentials

labels.name: Feature
labels.description: New capability, or an improvement to how something already works

items.body:
I've been setting up pulumi to use azure keyvault.

Prior to this I had my CI (on azure devops) build something like this:
```yaml
- script: |
    export PATH=$PATH:$HOME/.pulumi/bin
    pulumi login --cloud-url azblob://pulumi-state
    pulumi stack select test
    pulumi preview --diff
  displayName: run pulumi
  workingDirectory: src
  failOnStderr: true
  continueOnError: false
  env:
    ARM_CLIENT_ID: $(client_id)
    ARM_CLIENT_SECRET: $(client_secret)
    ARM_TENANT_ID: $(tenant_id)
    ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: $(subscriptionId)
    AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT: $(storage_account)
    AZURE_STORAGE_KEY: $(storage_account_key)
    PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE: $(pulumi_config_passphrase)
```

I decided to move away from using passphrase, and use --secrets-provider. Created a stack fine, using the secrets provider, used my own user on azure to do that (just local commands).

However, now when I was trying to select the stack on the CI just using service principal authentication, pipeline is not able to authenticate against keyvault.

The error I'm getting is this `error: getting secrets manager: secrets (code=InvalidArgument): azure.BearerAuthorizer#WithAuthorization: Failed to refresh the Token for request to https://somekeyvault.vault.azure.net/keys/keyname/someid/decrypt?api-version=7.0: StatusCode=400 -- Original Error: adal: Refresh request failed. Status Code = '400'. Response body: {"error":"invalid_request","error_description":"Identity not found"}
`
That's without changing the above pipeline.

I've resolved the issue by authenticating with az cli as well as just passing sp credentials to pulumi.
```yaml
- script: |
    az login --service-principal -u $(client_id) -p $(client_secret) --tenant $(tenant_id)
    export PATH=$PATH:$HOME/.pulumi/bin
    pulumi login --cloud-url azblob://pulumi-state
    pulumi stack select test
    pulumi preview --diff
  displayName: run pulumi
  workingDirectory: src
  failOnStderr: true
  continueOnError: false
  env:
    ARM_CLIENT_ID: $(client_id)
    ARM_CLIENT_SECRET: $(client_secret)
    ARM_TENANT_ID: $(tenant_id)
    ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: $(subscriptionId)
    AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT: $(storage_account)
    AZURE_STORAGE_KEY: $(storage_account_key)
    AZURE_KEYVAULT_AUTH_VIA_CLI: true
```

The [documentation](https://www.pulumi.com/docs/intro/concepts/config/#azure-key-vault) specifies that it should use Azure Environment authentication, which in my case should just use Client credentials just like what pulumi is using, however that is not the case.

items.title: SFL-0039: sink: per-org Loki tenant fan-out (X-Scope-OrgID routing) for multi-org isolation

labels.name: followup
labels.description: Deferred work for future agents to pick up

milestone.title: Feature roadmap — operator ergonomics & platform capabilities

items.body:
Legacy ID: SFL-0039

- Created: 2026-08-14T16:58:00Z
- Updated: unknown
- Original status: To Do
- Milestone: Feature roadmap — operator ergonomics & platform capabilities (m-4)
- Board file: `backlog/tasks/sfl-0039 - sink-per-org-Loki-tenant-fan-out-X-Scope-OrgID-routing-for-multi-org-isolation.md`

## Description

## What

Multi-org ingestion (`#31`) shares exactly one Loki tenant across every configured org. There is no way to route each org's entries to its own tenant, and no way to express the intent in config.

Current shape:

- `LokiConfig` holds a single `tenant_id` (`src/sf2loki/config.py:931-936`) alongside a single `url`/`auth_token(_file)`; `SinkConfig` exposes exactly one `loki` block (`src/sf2loki/config.py:983-984`).
- `OrgConfig` carries only `name`, `salesforce`, `sources` (`src/sf2loki/config.py:1298-1322`). It is a `StrictModel` (`extra="forbid"`), so an `orgs[].sink` key is rejected at load time rather than ignored.
- `LokiSink` builds one static header set at construction (`src/sf2loki/sinks/loki/sink.py:112` calling `_build_headers`, `src/sf2loki/sinks/loki/sink.py:120-131`): Basic auth with `tenant_id` as the username when `auth_token` is set, otherwise a single `X-Scope-OrgID: <tenant_id>` header. `_post` always posts to `self._cfg.url` with `{**self._headers, **content_headers}` (`src/sf2loki/sinks/loki/sink.py:203-207`), so both tenant and URL are process-wide constants.
- The composition root builds one sink and gives it to one pipeline: `src/sf2loki/app.py:922` and `src/sf2loki/app.py:1033-1041`. `doctor` (`src/sf2loki/doctor.py:362`) and `backfill` (`src/sf2loki/backfill.py:740`) each build their own single `LokiSink` the same way.
- Documented as a limitation: `README.md:342-347` ("the sink, state store, coordinator, and service settings stay shared … one Loki tenant") and `docs/architecture.md:222` ("one shared Loki sink").

Everything needed to partition already exists. `OrgSource` injects an `org` stream label (plus per-org `sf_org_id`/`environment`) into every non-`checkpoint_only` entry (`src/sf2loki/sources/org_adapter.py:110-114`), `org` is in `ALLOWED_LABELS` (`src/sf2loki/sinks/loki/labels.py:7`), and checkpoint keys are already prefixed `org=<name>:` via `OrgCheckpointView`, so per-key commit ordering is unaffected by splitting a batch on org. The Loki push API takes the tenant per request, so per-tenant routing needs no new protocol support — only per-request header selection (multi-tenant Loki) or a per-org client when `url`/token differ (separate Grafana Cloud stacks).

## Why it matters

An MSP or ISV partner ingesting five customer orgs through one process lands all five customers' Salesforce security events (login, API usage, session, Apex) in one Loki tenant. Consequences:

- Tenant-level isolation is unavailable. Anyone with query access to that Loki tenant reads every customer's login and API events. Label-based access control on the `org` label is the only remaining control and it is not available on every Loki deployment.
- Per-customer retention, ingest limits, and per-tenant usage attribution are impossible — those are tenant-scoped in Loki, not label-scoped.
- The operator is forced back to N processes with N configs and N state volumes, which is exactly the cost `#31` removed.

## Proposed approach

Add an optional per-org sink override that falls back to the shared sink, and dispatch batches by the `org` label inside the sink seam.

1. Config: new `OrgSinkOverride(StrictModel)` with `tenant_id: str | None`, `url: str | None`, `auth_token: SecretStr | None`, `auth_token_file: Path | None`; add `sink: OrgSinkOverride | None = None` to `OrgConfig` (`src/sf2loki/config.py:1298-1322`). Unset fields inherit from `sink.loki`, so `tenant_id`-only is the common case (one Loki, N tenants) and `url` + token is the separate-stack case. Everything else (encoding, compression, batch, egress, `structured_metadata_fields`, static `labels`) stays deployment-wide — do not fork those, they feed the pipeline and the governor, not the request.
2. Validation, as a model validator on `Config`: reject `orgs[].sink` when `orgs` is empty (single-org), and reject `auth_token` together with `auth_token_file` per override (mirror the existing `LokiConfig` secret-file resolution path so `*_file` reads go through the same loader).
3. Sink: add `src/sf2loki/sinks/loki/fanout.py` with a `FanOutSink` implementing the `Sink` protocol (`src/sf2loki/sinks/base.py:33-36`), holding `{org_name: LokiSink}` plus a default `LokiSink`. `push()` partitions `batch.entries` on `entry.labels.get("org")` (order-preserving, one dict pass), then awaits each sub-batch's `LokiSink.push` sequentially. Entries with no `org` label, or an `org` value with no configured entry, go to the default sink — a mapped-org-without-config situation cannot occur because org names come from the same config list, so assert it at build time rather than at push time. `aclose()` closes every distinct `httpx.AsyncClient`. Reuse one shared client for overrides that do not change `url` (headers are per-request), and create a client per distinct `url`.
4. Error semantics: a `PermanentSinkError` from one sub-batch must not discard the others — catch it per sub-batch, count `loki_entries_dropped` with the existing reason tag, and continue, matching the 413-split behaviour at `src/sf2loki/sinks/loki/sink.py:263-288`. A `RetryableSinkError` from any sub-batch propagates after the remaining sub-batches have been attempted, because the pipeline retries the whole batch (`src/sf2loki/app.py:456-470`). That re-sends already-delivered sub-batches; this is the existing at-least-once contract and Loki drops exact duplicate (stream, timestamp, line) entries, so document it rather than adding cross-call state.
5. Composition root: at `src/sf2loki/app.py:922`, build the fan-out sink when any org declares `sink`, otherwise keep constructing the plain `LokiSink` so single-org and shared-tenant multi-org wiring stay byte-identical. Leave `EgressGovernor` (`src/sf2loki/app.py:1031`) deployment-wide — per-org budgets are a separate change.
6. Observability: `sf2loki_loki_push` / `sf2loki_loki_bytes_pushed` (`src/sf2loki/obs/metrics.py:312-330`) stay unlabelled to avoid breaking the shipped dashboards and rule pack. Instead, include the org name in the auth-failure and drop log lines emitted from the per-org `LokiSink` (`src/sf2loki/sinks/loki/sink.py:290-300`), e.g. by passing an optional `label: str` to `LokiSink` used only in log context.
7. `doctor`: `_check_loki` (`src/sf2loki/doctor.py:358-385`) probes one sink. When per-org sinks are configured, probe the sink for the selected `--org` (doctor already operates on one org) and name it in the result message. `backfill` (`src/sf2loki/backfill.py:740`) likewise builds the selected org's sink.
8. Docs: replace the "one Loki tenant" statements at `README.md:342-347` and `docs/architecture.md:222`, extend `examples/presets/multi-org.yaml` with a commented per-org tenant example, and run `just gen-config` so `config.example.yaml` / `docs/config-reference.md` / the Helm chart's generated config stay drift-gate clean (`tests/test_config_artifacts_drift.py`).

---

Imported from GitHub issue ``#123`` on 2026-08-14, when this repo migrated from GitHub Issues to Backlog.md. The original issue has been deleted; its verbatim body, labels and comments are preserved in `archive/issues-dump.json` (`jq '.[] | select(.number == 123)' archive/issues-dump.json`).

<sub>Filed from the 2026-07-30 full-repo audit (11 finder lanes + adversarial verification per finding).</sub>

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 `orgs[].sink` accepts `tenant_id` alone and inherits `url`/auth from `sink.loki`; unit test in `tests/test_config.py` asserts the resolved per-org sink settings.
- [ ] AC2 Config rejects `orgs[].sink` when no `orgs` are configured, and rejects `auth_token` + `auth_token_file` together in one override; both pinned by `pytest.raises(ValidationError)` tests.
- [ ] AC3 `auth_token_file` in an override is read through the same secret-file resolution as `sink.loki.auth_token_file`; test writes a temp token file and asserts the header value.
- [ ] AC4 `FanOutSink.push` sends one request per distinct org, each with that org's `X-Scope-OrgID` (or Basic-auth username), verified with an `httpx.MockTransport` capturing requests: a batch of entries labelled `org=a`/`org=b` produces two requests with the two tenant ids and disjoint line sets.
- [ ] AC5 Entries with no `org` label route to the default sink; test asserts one request with the shared tenant.
- [ ] AC6 A `PermanentSinkError` on one org's sub-batch does not prevent the other orgs' sub-batches from being pushed, and increments `loki_entries_dropped` only for the failed sub-batch's entries.
- [ ] AC7 A `RetryableSinkError` on one org's sub-batch propagates to the caller after the other sub-batches have been attempted; test asserts both requests were made and the exception surfaced.
- [ ] AC8 Distinct `url` overrides get distinct clients and `aclose()` closes each exactly once (no double-close, no leak); test counts closes.
- [ ] AC9 `App.build` produces a plain `LokiSink` when no org declares `sink`, and a `FanOutSink` when one does; test asserts the sink type for both configs.
- [ ] AC10 Checkpoint commit still happens once per flush after all sub-pushes succeed; test asserts no checkpoint advances when one org's sub-batch raises `RetryableSinkError`.
- [ ] AC11 `doctor` writes its probe line to the selected org's tenant when per-org sinks are configured; test asserts the request header.
- [ ] AC12 `README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` no longer claim a single shared Loki tenant is the only option; `examples/presets/multi-org.yaml` shows the per-org tenant form.
- [ ] AC13 `just gen-config` re-run and `just gate` green (ruff, mypy --strict, pytest), including the config-artifact drift gate.

## Definition of done

- [ ] just gate is green (ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy src + pytest) — run it, don't assert it
- [ ] just gen-config run and its output committed, if config.py changed (CI drift gate fails otherwise)
- [ ] committed straight to main with a conventional-commit message, and pushed

## Links

- Reference: `https://github.com/rknightion/sf2loki/issues/123`
